title: China Built the World's Longest Desert Road — 446 km Across Shifting Sand | China Travel Expert
description:
China ran a paved highway straight across a sea of moving sand — and then fought to keep it from being buried.

The Tarim Desert Highway crosses the Taklamakan in Xinjiang. Of its ~552 km, about 446 km run through uninhabited shifting dunes — the longest road across that kind of desert anywhere on Earth. Because dunes creep and swallow roads, engineers planted a living shelterbelt of drought-tough shrubs that runs roughly 436 km beside the tarmac, 70-plus metres wide, watered by wells pumped up from beneath the desert. Crews live in stations spaced along the route just to keep the sand back.

🧭 Expert Tip: if you ever cross it, go with an experienced local driver and a full tank — there are long stretches with no fuel, no water and no signal.
